questions.stem: Rice costing ₹8/kg is mixed with rice costing ₹12/kg to get a mixture at ₹10/kg. The mixing ratio is:
questions.explanation: A is correct. By alligation: cheaper:dearer = (dearer − mean):(mean − cheaper) = (12−10):(10−8) = 2:2 = 1:1.

questions.stem: A milkman mixes 5 L of milk with 3 L of water. What fraction of the mixture is milk?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Total mixture = 5+3 = 8 L. Fraction of milk = 5/8.

questions.stem: A vessel contains 80 L of pure milk. 20 L is removed and replaced with water. What percentage of the mixture is milk?
questions.explanation: B is correct. After removal and replacement: milk = 80−20 = 60 L in 80 L total. Percentage = 60/80 × 100 = 75%.

questions.stem: In what ratio should a 20% alcohol solution be mixed with a 50% alcohol solution to get a 30% solution?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Alligation: 20% solution : 50% solution = (50−30):(30−20) = 20:10 = 2:1.

questions.stem: A container has 40 L of milk-water mixture in ratio 3:1. How much water must be added to make it 3:2?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Milk = 30 L, Water = 10 L. Required ratio 3:2 means Water = (2/3) × Milk = 20 L. Additional water needed = 20−10 = 10 L.

questions.stem: How many kg of sugar at ₹5/kg must be mixed with 30 kg of sugar at ₹7/kg to get a mixture worth ₹6/kg?
questions.explanation: D is correct. Alligation: ₹5 sugar : ₹7 sugar = (7−6):(6−5) = 1:1. Equal quantities → need 30 kg of ₹5 sugar to mix with 30 kg of ₹7 sugar.

questions.stem: A vessel has 40 L of milk. 8 L is removed and replaced with water — this process is done 3 times. What fraction of the mixture is milk?
questions.explanation: C is correct. After each replacement, milk fraction × (1 − 8/40) = fraction × (4/5). After 3 replacements: milk fraction = (4/5)³ = 64/125. Short Trick: repeated replacement formula = (1 − removed/total)^n.

questions.stem: Two acid solutions have concentrations 10% and 25%. In what ratio should they be mixed to get a 20% acid solution?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Alligation: 10% : 25% = (25−20):(20−10) = 5:10 = 1:2. Use more of the stronger solution when the desired concentration is closer to the stronger.

questions.stem: 40 L of a wine-water mixture has wine and water in ratio 3:1. How much wine should be added to make it 4:1?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Wine = 30 L, Water = 10 L. Target ratio 4:1 → Water stays at 10 L → Wine needed = 4×10 = 40 L. Add 40−30 = 10 L of wine.

questions.stem: Two gold alloys contain gold at 60% and 80% respectively. In what ratio must they be mixed to get an alloy with 74% gold?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Alligation: 60% alloy : 80% alloy = (80−74):(74−60) = 6:14 = 3:7. The 60% alloy is much further from 74% than the 80% alloy, so we use less of it.
